editorial.tldr: Anthropic answered Zhipu's GLM-5.3-Flash price undercut with a 75% cache-price cut on Fable/Mythos 5.1 in early September. On Sep 22 Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI answered within about an hour with GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, turning the pricing skirmish into a same-day flagship race.
editorial.whats_new: Anthropic followed the launch with two of its own posts on Opus 5.5's economics: a Sep 24 case for why longer, context-heavy coding sessions shaped its design, then a Sep 25 breakdown of what a Claude Code task actually costs and which settings move the bill.
editorial.why_it_matters: Whatever Claude-vs-GPT cost model you pinned evals to last week is now stale -- Opus 5.5's AWS availability, its context-heavy pricing design, and the wider 40-50% price cuts all change per-token math across both labs.
editorial.take_for_builders: Re-run your Claude vs. GPT cost model against Opus 5.5's AWS Bedrock pricing and the newly-cut competitor rates -- don't assume last week's per-token numbers still hold.

status.detail: Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol/Luna's same-day launch escalated into board-wide 40-50% price cuts by Sep 23, with Opus 5.5 now live on AWS Bedrock; by Sep 24-25 Anthropic followed up with its own guidance on the model's context-heavy design and per-task costs.
